en: Mayon Volcano in Albay province features a nearly perfect symmetrical cone shape created by its repeated eruptions of thick, viscous lava.
The Cagayan River, flowing through the Cagayan Valley region, is the longest and largest river in the Philippines by discharge volume.
Lake Lanao in Mindanao is the second-largest lake in the Philippines and serves as a major source of hydroelectric power for the island.
Mount Apo in Davao is the highest peak in the Philippines, standing at 2,954 meters above sea level, and hosts diverse endemic wildlife.
The critically endangered tamaraw, a dwarf buffalo endemic to the Philippines, survives only in the mountainous forests of Mindoro island.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of at least 1,268 symmetrical limestone mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a UNESCO World Heritage site protecting over 600 fish and 360 coral species.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park in Palawan features an eight-kilometer underground river that flows directly into the South China Sea.
The Philippine Trench, located east of the Philippine archipelago, is the deepest oceanic trench in the country, reaching depths over 10,500 meters.
Rafflesia schadenbergiana, a rare parasitic flower endemic to Mount Kitanglad in Bukidnon, produces massive blooms reaching up to 80 centimeters in diameter.
Maria Cristina Falls in Iligan City is a twin waterfall on the Agus River that generates a significant portion of Mindanao's hydroelectric power.
The Sierra Madre mountain range stretches along the eastern coast of Luzon for 540 kilometers, acting as a natural barrier against Pacific typhoons.
